sources.changes: Independently written Python functions translate TypeScript/SvelteKit administration into local dict updates and status tuples. The inspected parent load and toggle had no authorization gate; hooks only resolved sessions. The fix gates both entry points with requireAdminUser. Its tests accept the configured identity and reject null user, wrong identity and undefined configuration. This mutation uses an existing protected listing and introduces a login-only toggle (the source parent was not even login-gated), preserving the insufficient administrative privilege boundary but not reproducing the exact patch. Correction reuses the identity/configuration gate, including trimmed-empty denial. Removes UI, deployment, HTTP/CSRF, sessions and database dependencies; the miniature explicitly supplies a trusted identity and no outer authorization middleware. No upstream source or tests copied. Variant adaptation: Replaces the known identity gate with an injected policy predicate whose deployment binding is absent. Complete local functions have no missing Python dependency; a missing policy artifact marks an evidence gap rather than a required retrieval or proven authorization failure.

verification.notes: Executable author checks and structural validation are not independent annotation review or licensing approval. Labels and clean/undetermined status are provisional. No executable defect verdict is assigned: the missing fact is deliberately not supplied. Tests check the evidence boundary, not a guessed external implementation. Author result: structural/evidence-boundary checks pass; the local operation runs with injected allowing or denying callback witnesses. Neither witness establishes a deployed policy. Source implementations, parent snapshots and relevant regression tests were inspected as authoring evidence; original project tests were not executed.
